extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readership and policymakers interested in postwar food and agricultural policy
extracted.subtask_description: A news report summarizing an international conference's findings and recommendations on food, nutrition, agricultural production, distribution, and proposed international commodity arrangements in the immediate postwar period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governments declare intent to secure more and better food
rubrics_metrics.description: Governments represented should declare to their own people and to one another their intention to secure more and better food for the people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The declaration is a principal recommendation of the conference and is tied to public policy and mutual commitments among governments; it signals political will and underpins other measures to increase food supply and improve nutrition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust production programs with foresight to long-term requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Production programs must be guided by foresight so that temporary heavy demand for energy foods during shortages does not lead to over-production once shortages are overcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actual programs should be drawn up to suit the particular circumstances of each country; governments should steer producers to alter production in accordance with long-term requirements rather than short-term market swings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set intermediate, region-specific nutrition goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt intermediate goals that can be progressively raised as conditions improve and that differ from region to region according to climate, taste, social habits and other circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because ultimate objectives (adequate nutrition for all) are global and long-term, practical measures require intermediate, locally adapted targets. These are primarily matters for individual governments to determine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize immediate post-liberation food relief
rubrics_metrics.description: In the short term after liberation of occupied territories, priority must be to reach freedom from hunger in areas devastated by war, with immediate demand for cereals and other energy-maintaining foods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until lands can produce harvests themselves, relief and imports should focus on staples that satisfy hunger and maintain human energy; relief planning should reflect the expected duration of agricultural inactivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase production of 'protective' foods and adjust production mix
rubrics_metrics.description: New and existing production would have to be adjusted to secure more of those 'protective' foods necessary to good health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conference agreed on broad standards of nutrition and that production programs should secure not just calories but a nutritional balance; adjustments involve policy guidance to producers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote new agricultural development in unproductive areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Some presently unproductive parts of the world could be brought into agricultural production if appropriate measures were applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conference recommended measures for development (e.g., land improvement, drainage, farming methods) to increase potential agricultural area and output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address overcrowding on land by increasing productivity or diversifying employment
rubrics_metrics.description: In some rich-potential areas, overcrowding of farmers on the land impedes development; while farming improvements can help, industry development or emigration may be the only measures likely to offer significant contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approaches include improved methods of farming, drainage, land improvement; where land cannot absorb population, develop industry or encourage movement to other areas as part of policy mix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure people have means to acquire food — tackle poverty and employment
rubrics_metrics.description: It is useless to produce food unless men and nations have means to acquire it for consumption; poverty is the first cause of malnutrition and hunger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Progress requires raising general employment levels through national and international action; distribution and purchasing power are as important as production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize interdependence of employment, industrial development, currencies, investment and trade policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Freedom from want of food depends on progress in employment, character and extent of industrial development, management of currencies, direction of national and international investment, and national policies toward foreign trade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conference Section III emphasized that these economic factors are closely interdependent and must be addressed together to improve distribution and assure adequate returns to producers and buying power for consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote economic expansion to achieve freedom from want
rubrics_metrics.description: Freedom from want of food cannot be fully achieved without a balanced and worldwide expansion of economic activity; governments and authorities should take action individually and in concert to secure this objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The conference did not prescribe detailed policies but declared economic expansion fundamental and urged cooperative action among nations.

rubrics_metrics.name: International commodity arrangements should eliminate excessive short-term price movements
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrangements for control of staple foodstuffs entering international trade should aim to eliminate excessive short-term movements in prices, mitigate inflationary or deflationary movements, and facilitate production adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The objective is to prevent economic dislocation and to allow producers and consumers to plan; the conference discussed buffer stocks and other mechanisms to stabilize markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider role of buffer stocks in commodity arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: (Question a) The place which buffer stocks should occupy in arrangements for staples must be considered when designing international commodity controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Buffer stocks are explicitly mentioned as a means to stabilize prices and supply; the conference recommended further discussion on their scope and functioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide whether to include production regulation within arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: (Question b) Consider how far it would be necessary to include regulation of production within general commodity arrangements to achieve desired objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The conference directed discussion at the principle level; details of production control versus market measures were left for further deliberation among governments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure effective representation of consumers as well as producers in arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any international commodity arrangements should include effective representation of consumers as well as producers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The point stresses fairness and balance in designing rules and institutions so that consumer interests (affordable food) are represented alongside producer interests (adequate returns).

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish an interim commission and prepare declarations/agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: An interim commission to be established in Washington should prepare declarations or agreements for consideration by governments and authorities to implement the conference's sense regarding nutrition and standards of living.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The interim commission's task is preparatory: to draft principles and possible arrangements for later governmental negotiation and detailed agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a permanent international organization for food and agriculture
rubrics_metrics.description: The nations represented should establish a permanent organization in the field of food and agriculture to act as a center of information and advice on nutrition and standards of living.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This organization would coordinate statistics, advise on policy, and help operate commodity arrangements in light of agreed broad principles; the conference saw it as necessary infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide coordinating machinery and statistics service for commodity arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever the nature of eventual arrangements for individual commodities, machinery (including a statistics service) would be needed for coordinating their operations in the light of broad principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective operation of international arrangements requires administrative and analytical capacity (data, monitoring, coordination) to implement and adjust measures such as buffer stocks or production rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continue international discussion to formulate broad governing principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Further international discussion should take place with a view to formulating broad principles to govern the formulation and operation of future commodity arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The conference recommended that detailed scope and functions of arrangements be worked out in further negotiations between representatives of participating governments, recognizing the need to relate such organizations to other national and international bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governmentscknowledge mutual obligation to raise nutrition and improve agricultural efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Governments and authorities represented should recognize their obligation to their own people and to one another to raise levels of nutrition and standards of living and to improve the efficiency of agricultural production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a normative conclusion of the conference intended to guide national policy and international cooperation; the interim commission was asked to prepare declarations reflecting this responsibility.
